_README: Per-car overrides for re/tools/bake_td5_car_paint.py. Everything here is a
JUDGEMENT CALL that no measurement can settle, so it lives in data instead of
being buried in thresholds. Edit a value and re-run the baker for that car:
python re/tools/bake_td5_car_paint.py <code>
paint_all_varying (default false)
Normally only the PRIMARY paint is recoloured: a texel that moves between
the four factory skins but does not follow the primary paint is treated as
deliberate art (a stripe, a flame, a second body colour) and keeps what it
shipped with.
That policy assumes the four skins are the SAME car in four colours. On a
handful of cars they are not -- they are four different LIVERIES (mus and
fhm have flames only on skins 1/3, cat's skin 3 is a green/yellow two-tone,
chv has flames on skin 0 and racing stripes on 2/3). There the primary paint
covers only part of the body and the rest stays at SKIN 0's colour, which on
a repainted car reads as a white hood or a red nose next to a blue body.
Set true to recolour EVERY texel the four paints move (minus the chrome /
specular-dominated ones, which stay protected either way). The car then
takes one coherent colour and loses its flames/stripes. Set false to keep
the livery and accept the patches.
Chosen below: true where the leftover reads as a defect (a plain car with a
stray white or red panel), false where the livery IS the car's identity.

mus.why: '68 Mustang: skins 0/1 both plain white, 2 dark, 3 magenta with flames. The flame texels left the HOOD and ROCKER white on a repainted car -- a hard cut, not a livery.

fhm.why: '68 Mustang HR: skin 1 purple+flames, skin 3 a yellow/cyan two-tone. Left the NOSE and FRONT FENDER white against a repainted body.

128.why: SPEED 12: an IRIDESCENT paint (purple / teal / black / silver). The flank where it shifts hue goes achromatic in skin 3, so the chrome guard dropped it and a repainted car kept a magenta streak down the right flank plus a pink patch at the nose. Coverage 89.4% -> 97.3%; claimed-but-not-moving only +202 texels, so no chrome or lamp was swallowed. There is no livery here to lose -- the gradient IS the paint.

cat.why: Super 7: skin 3 is a green body with a yellow nose, so the nose fits no single paint and kept skin 0's red. Lowest paint contrast of the roster (Pcon 0.51).

chv.why: '70 Chevelle: the FLAMES are the car. Skin 0's yellow flames over the chosen colour read as intentional, so the primary-only policy is right here.

hot.why: '69 Camaro HR: a genuine two-tone plus red pinstripes. Keeping them is the point of the car.

cob.why: Cobra: the twin bonnet stripes are present in all four schemes, just in different colours. Keep them.
